title: Archive through December 19, 2002 - Anonymous (Thursday, December 19, 2002 - 04:17 pm)
content: I Accidentally overdosed on pain meds I was given because I had broken my left ankle, leg bone had to have surgery (plate and screws were put in). I also had nerve damage (Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy 3rd stage) I was in excruciating pain (accident happened June 4th, 2001). On July 12th 2002 at 1am my husband found me in bed, blue, making a gurgling sound, not breathing just exhaling. He called 911 and started full CPR. I had to be shocked twice in my bedroom, bagged. I flatlined in the ambulance in my driveway, Paramedics had to start chest massages again off and on for about 35 minutes. At the hospital I was put on a respirator and transferred to a trauma I.C.U. The E.R. Doc. told my husband she didn’t know if I would live or not or if I did, what the extent of brain damage I would have. That it would be at least 48hrs. before they would know. The CAT scan results were good. I woke up 15 hrs later (to the amazement of the ICU Doctor) confused but, in good health. I was taken off the respirator a few hours later. The ICU Doctor told me and my family that I definitely had some help from God. That he had never seen anyone in the shape I was in come out of it as early as I did and totally unscathed. I was given a paralyzing drug to stop my thrashing before I was transferred by ambulance to the Trauma Center of a different hospital. Okay, this is hard for me (I am crying), this is what I dreamed? While I was unconscious. In the beginning I was walking somewhere and it was dark, it looks like a different Town or City. Someone is with me but I cannot see who. I now feel I cannot breath nor move, I am terrified, then I calm down and I am thinking where am I. At first I tell myself I must be dreaming. I think I am in a movie theater. It is so dark I can see nothing. Sounds crazy I know, but then I realize or I am thinking I have died. I am now in a house or building or something, there are other people but they do not notice me or speak to me. I am thinking that this is some sort of waiting room or purgatory. The noise I hear I cannot describe it is so loud, deafening! I am suddenly outside the place looking at some water, a lake I think, there are what looks like little demons of some sort, but they don’t scare me I ignore them. Then I am then in a different room with others and again I feel like I am waiting to go to heaven and the noise is still so loud. I am confused. I don’t feel I belong here and I am wanting God. I suddenly began to move (sort of like floating) towards a tunnel, the others I sense are mad because I am going ahead of them. I am sucked up into a tunnel that feels like and I get the sudden knowledge that I am in a birth canal heading toward a light, it is very quick and when I get to the light I see a woman in an ambulance. I am thinking that I am to be reincarnated as her child. I have never believed in reincarnation. She is African American and I am white. (I know that I am white and I am thinking how can this be how can I become her child now). The race difference doesn't matter to me. I am thinking she is a nice person I would like to be her child. But then I have a baby in my arms I know that it is her child and at first I am thinking that I am bringing her, her baby. I know that I am taking her baby to Heaven. I go through the light with her child and I come back through the light and now I am walking down the tunnel again I have a little girl of about five years of age holding my right hand and walking with me. I pass two women and it is the first time someone notices me, they smile. I pass a man who looks at me and says angrily why does she get to go! I ignore him I don’t know who he is referring to, the little girl or me and I don’t care. I go through the birth canal feeling again (it is painful both times) towards a bright light. I go through with the little girl when I come back through she isn't with me. I am scared because I don't know where she is, then I realize she is with Jesus. I feel good that she is with Jesus, but I feel sorrow for her mother. Then I walked back passed the three people and I myself. I am walking towards a light there is a woman with long dark hair in the light I am thinking that she is my grandmother only she isn't old anymore. She looks at me and tells me "It’s not your time, it just isn't your time". She is smiling. Then I am seeing a woman (she is beautiful with long brown hair) at the end of my hospital bed, and I can see myself lying in the bed, I am confused, I look at her and I am speaking to her and I don't know how because I can see myself in the hospital bed with tubes down my throat, hooked to machines. I am trying to convey to her the dream I had but she already knows and asks me while smiling "did you see the light". I answer “yes”. I look at myself in the hospital bed, then look back towards her and she is gone. Then I wake up. I can't move yet because of the paralyzing drug. I hear my husbands voice but I can't raise my eyelids to see him. When I can move he realizes I am awake and tells me I am in the ICU at the hospital and that I overdosed on the medication, I don’t know how but I already knew what had happened to me. My leg that had been extremely swollen and red and purple and glassy for the passed 13 months including the day of July 12th from the nerve damage was now perfectly normal! No pain, just normal! My Doctor had no explanation other than by the grace of God. I can't stop thinking about it. When I told my husband about the "dream" he asked me if I could think of him or our kids. I didn't. I could only think that I didn't belong there. Was it a near death experience or was I dreaming? I am very confused. I wish someone could help me understand one way or another. I have also suffered from Cluster headaches for the passed 22yrs once a year for 6 to 12wks. I was expecting them in November this year. I didn't get them. I don't know if I will get them but I am thinking that they are gone forever now. Any info. would be greatly appreciated. Thanks for listening. P.S., Please, I don't want anyone to think that I was or am a drug addict, I am not. It was a terrible accident and I am thankful to God for my second chance.

diagnosis.diagnosis_raw: Broken left ankle/leg bone requiring surgery with plate and screws; nerve damage (Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy 3rd stage); accidental overdose on pain meds with cardiac/respiratory arrest; history of cluster headaches.
diagnosis.disease_name: Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy (Complex Regional Pain Syndrome), 3rd stage; accidental opioid/pain medication overdose with cardiac arrest; cluster headaches (episodic).
diagnosis.severity_description: Excruciating pain; prolonged swelling/red-purple discoloration for 13 months; overdose with prolonged resuscitation/flatline risk; concern for brain damage.
diagnosis.prognosis_given: ER doctor told husband she didn’t know if she would live or, if she lived, what the extent of brain damage would be; would take at least 48 hours to know.
diagnosis.quality_of_life_impact: Excruciating pain; leg extremely swollen and red/purple/glassy for 13 months.
diagnosis.disease_duration_before_healing: About 13 months of severe RSD symptoms before July 12, 2002

treatment.treatments_raw: Orthopedic surgery with plate and screws after fracture; prescribed pain medications (accidental overdose); emergency resuscitation (CPR, defibrillation, bagging/ventilation), respirator/ICU care; paralyzing drug for thrashing; transfer to trauma center.
treatment.surgery_type: Surgery for broken left ankle/leg with plate and screws.

remission_outcome.time_to_remission_raw: Immediately upon awakening after overdose/ICU event (leg was normal when she woke up 15 hours later).
remission_outcome.verification_detail: Upon awakening in ICU, the previously swollen/red/purple/glassy leg from 13 months of RSD was 'perfectly normal' with no pain; doctor had no explanation other than 'by the grace of God.' ICU doctor also stated she had 'help from God' given recovery from arrest; CAT scan reported good.
remission_outcome.physician_quote: ICU Doctor told me and my family that I definitely had some help from God. That he had never seen anyone in the shape I was in come out of it as early as I did and totally unscathed.

positive_emotion_practices: expressing thankfulness to God for a second chance
turner_factors.spiritual_practices_raw: Strong attribution to God/grace; desire for God during the experience; references to Jesus; belief in divine help.

pre_illness_state.patient_causal_belief: RSD/nerve damage caused by the accident; overdose was an accident (not addiction).

existential_shift.transformation_narrative: During unconsciousness she believed she had died, felt she did not belong there, wanted God, encountered a figure she identified as her grandmother who told her it was not her time, and later associated the child with Jesus; afterward she framed survival and healing as a second chance and grace of God.
existential_shift.pivot_point_description: Encounter with grandmother-like figure saying: 'It’s not your time, it just isn't your time.'
existential_shift.transformation_timing: Experience occurred while unconscious; physical improvement noticed upon awakening.

anomalous_experience.experience_description: During unconsciousness after overdose/cardiac arrest, experienced dark 'waiting' spaces, loud noise, tunnel/birth-canal sensation toward a light, interactions with entities/people, sense of taking a baby/child through the light, and encounter with grandmother-like figure stating it was not her time; later perceived a woman at the end of the hospital bed asking 'did you see the light' while she saw her body in bed.
anomalous_experience.experience_timing: During overdose-related unconsciousness while on ventilator/ICU care (July 12, 2002).

validation.statistical_improbability_notes: Prolonged resuscitation/flatline with rapid awakening and no reported deficits; abrupt normalization of long-standing stage 3 RSD symptoms is presented as unexpected by physicians, but documentation is limited to narrative and physician comments.
validation.extraction_notes: No objective RSD diagnostic criteria, imaging, or follow-up documentation provided; cluster headache remission is speculative (she notes she 'didn't get them' yet and is unsure if gone).

analysis.case_summary: After an accidental overdose of prescribed pain medication following orthopedic surgery and long-standing stage 3 Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy, the patient experienced cardiac/respiratory arrest with prolonged resuscitation and an NDE-like experience. She awakened about 15 hours later with unexpectedly good neurologic recovery and reported immediate resolution of severe RSD symptoms in the affected leg; physicians reportedly had no explanation other than divine help/grace.
key_healing_factors: Near-death experience with a 'not your time' message
Strong spiritual framing/attribution to God and Jesus
Strong immediate social support (husband initiating CPR; family present)
unique_features: Abrupt resolution of long-standing stage 3 RSD/CRPS symptoms immediately after overdose/NDE
Prolonged resuscitation with rapid awakening and reportedly no deficits
NDE content includes birth-canal/tunnel sensation and escorting children through the light
analysis.analysis_notes: Primary remission-like outcome is resolution of RSD symptoms; cluster headache improvement is not yet confirmed as durable. Conventional emergency interventions were substantial, so this is not 'pure spontaneous' remission.
